thread:
zack: quick sync — sales wants a clearer story for p95 vs p99 for AcmeBank. they asked if we can hit p95=120ms and p99=350ms at their target qps (150) 

maya: do we have a recent profile for acme-like traffic? qps 150 with 16b models, seq len ~256, ~30% short prompts.

profiler-bot: profiling run 2026-03-10 for workload 'acme-like' attached: 
```
-- microbatch=1: p95=110ms p99=420ms throughput=155rps
-- microbatch=2: p95=140ms p99=380ms throughput=260rps
-- microbatch=4: p95=220ms p99=520ms throughput=420rps
KV warmup disabled
kernel=opt-attn-v2
```

diane: TL;DR: can hit p95=120ms at mb=1 but p99 is high (420ms) due to tail spikes from cold KV and occasional kernel fallback. At mb=2 p95 pushes above 120.

ellie_sales: Sales note — AcmeBank will accept a trade: p95=120ms firm, p99 negotiable up to 400ms but they'd like proof we can keep it under 400 in steady state. need a short bullet list of mitigations.

ravi_pm: can we offer a tiered SLA? e.g., p95=120ms GA, p99 90th-day target 400ms with dedicated pool + warmup?

zack: technical options: 1) keep microbatch=1 for this customer on dedicated pool (sacrifice throughput), 2) aggressive KV prefill + prefix caching, 3) kernel pinning to avoid fallback to unquantized path, 4) knob to limit concurrent requests per GPU to reduce head-of-line blocking.

maya: adding numbers — if we prefill KV for top-75% frequent prefixes, profiler shows p99 drop ~80ms avg (so 420 -> ~340). kernel pin avoids 30-60ms spikes. combined ~= 420-90 = 330ish.

diane: note regression we saw last week: a scheduler change increased p99 by ~60ms for mb=1 under bursty load. we've reverted in staging but need test plan.

zack: propose an onboarding config for AcmeBank: dedicated small pool (2 GPUs), microbatch=1, kernel-pin=opt-attn-v2, kv-prefill=true, max-inflight-per-gpu=12. Expected steady-state p95 ~110-125ms, p99 ~320-380ms based on current tests.

ellie_sales: sounds promising. they also asked about rollout: can we pilot this for a week and provide hourly SLO dashboard?

maya: yes — we can enable tracing and per-request token breakdown, plus p95/p99 dashboards. need a temporary eval key and metrics export.

ravi_pm: can we commit to automatic fallback if p99 > 420ms for 5 consecutive 5-min windows? fallback = route to larger instance or pause batching to microbatch=1?

diane: fallback plan: 1) increase kernel parallelism (if available), 2) switch to pinned kernel, 3) if still bad, scale up instance size or shift to dedicated higher-SKU. we should avoid toggling microbatch in-flight — that causes jitter.

zack: action items: @maya run controlled pilot with the proposed config for 24h and produce hourly p95/p99 + KV hit-rate graphs. @diane validate no regression in scheduler with this config. @ravi_pm draft SLA wording with the fallback carveouts. @ellie_sales confirm AcmeBank is ok with pilot.

ellie_sales: pinging Acme now, will confirm by EOD. :thumbsup:

profiler-bot: scheduled job started: pilot-profile-acme-2177774444. ETA 26h.

diane: note to engineering — include deterministic seed for load generator and inject cold-start windows to quantify worst-case tails. also capture kernel-fallback counts.

maya: will include those. also testing will run both with kv-prefill=true and false.

zack: one more ask from sales: they want a simple one-page doc explaining why p99 is higher and what we do to control it. maya, can you draft the doc with the perf numbers + mitigations? keep it non-technical.

maya: yep, I'll draft and share a short bullet doc.

ellie_sales: thanks all. if pilot metrics look good, we can move to contract amendment.

deploy-bot: note: no deploys to runtime clusters scheduled during pilot window (2026-03-11 00:00 -> 2026-03-12 00:00).

zack: thanks team. I'll follow up with an internal summary once maya posts the pilot results.

ellie_sales: FYI — Acme replied: ok to pilot, requested 24h notice before pilot start.
